newsitem.title: UK: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - LIRMA and derivatives.
newsitem.headline: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - LIRMA and derivatives.

text.p: THE PROTEUS COLUMN

The London International Insurance and Reinsurance Market Association is the latest to look at the issue of derivatives. The association is considering a mechanism to allow such instruments to be used in every sector of insurance, as opposed to the catastrophe side, where efforts on derivatives have so far been concentrated, in an attempt to even out the massive swings in pricing caused by the insurance cycle.
LIRMA hasn't yet decided how to proceed, but the fact that it is considering the issue at all is a relatively bold move.

The association has been looking for ways to show that it has come of age and is a real force in the market. If it is able to start sponsoring products used by its members, it will be providing a real and high profile service which could have a significant effect on the way the use of derivatives develops in insurance.

The trick will be to create something which the market can understand. Several conferences and papers have looked at the question of bringing capital markets into insurance, but market practitioners remain wary.

In part they fear their market being eroded, but a more important reason is the lack of understanding of what derivatives are. The area tends to be dominated by jargon and mathematics. Insurance people late in their careers are reluctant to grasp this new "rocket science" when they understand the traditional methods so well.
If LIRMA can bring something to the market which makes derivatives accessible, understandable and with wide market reach, it would be a significant achievement.
It would also be a considerable boost to LIRMA's own campaign to raise its profile and the profile of the London Market.

LIRMA is concerned about the issue of branding the London companies market, and making sure it is not seen as an adjunct to a dominant, newly reinvented Lloyd's of London. It wants to show it has something different to offer.

LIRMA remains reluctant to discuss any suggestion that it may merge with the other companies market body, the Institute of London Underwriters (ILU). But several market insiders feel that such a move is inevitable.

There are some problems with such an idea as Proteus has pointed out before, and it may be that an umbrella organisation formed between the ILU and LIRMA would be a necessary first step to pave the way for full merger.
